mathematics.assertion_tested: Constitutive energy identities and derivative benchmarks pass; regular constant-K spherical cores retain fixed cold mass and positive core radii under the declared smooth Plummer loading, with less contraction of the 1%, 5%, 10% and 50% mass shells than the defined circular-shell dust reference; a tighter solve agrees within tolerance.
mathematics.coefficient_domain: IEEE-754 double precision with adaptive ODE integration and scalar root finding
mathematics.conventions: d=rho/rho_q; x=r/sqrt(K/(4piG)); m=M/[4pi rho_q (K/(4piG))^(3/2)]; K spatially constant and frozen during equilibrium continuation; no Lambda term or responsive baryons in this isolated-core experiment.
inputs: Constitutive fixtures in test_material.py and hydrostatic benchmarks in test_equilibria.py
Initial d_c=5 and 20, each with its own fixed cold mass
Baryon mass fractions 0, 0.1, 0.3 relative to initial cold mass; nonzero cases have Plummer scale b/R_initial=0.1 or 0.3
Pressure-free boundary at d=1 with vacuum exterior; regular center; half-mass and half-central-density radii
Dust comparator solves r_final [m_shell+Mb(r_final)]=r_initial m_shell at cold-mass fractions 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5
non_claims: No halo formation inference from static equilibria
No rotating baryonic disc, point mass, full X48 zoom, or observed forest power calculation
No global nonlinear or nonradial interface stability theorem
No universal core radius, universal pressure cap, or microscopic derivation of a0
